one_line_description.quote: Grain captures and enriches your meetings, then delivers them to Claude, ChatGPT, or any AI tool so your agents can do the work.

has_public_api.quote: Connect Grain to your own tools and workflows with the Grain public API.

api_breadth.value: Read-write: recordings, transcripts, AI notes and action items, participants, tags, teams, meeting types; upload external recordings, update metadata, download video/transcripts (JSON, text, VTT, SRT), webhooks
api_breadth.quote: The Grain API lets developers read meeting data, manage recordings, and receive real-time events from Grain programmatically.

docs_url.quote: For the full technical reference, see developers.grain.com.

auth_methods.quote: OAuth2: the standard flow for building integrations to be used by any Grain user. Users authorize your application directly, and your app receives a token scoped to that user's data.

access_model.quote: Not for personal API access, which is available on every plan, including Free.

access_notes.value: Personal API access via Personal Access Token (PAT) is self-serve and available on every plan including Free; workspace-wide access via Workspace Access Token requires admin rights on Business or Enterprise plans; OAuth2 is required for integrations distributed to other Grain users.
access_notes.quote: Workspace API access is available on Business and Enterprise plans and requires admin access to generate.

official_mcp_server.quote: The Grain MCP (Model Context Protocol) connects Claude.ai (and other AI chat clients) directly to your meeting data in Grain, enabling powerful AI-powered individual workflows

rate_limits.value: 300 requests per minute per token; requests beyond the limit return 429 Too Many Requests (rate limit headers returned on each response)
rate_limits.quote: The API allows 300 requests per minute per token. Requests beyond this limit return a `429 Too Many Requests` response. Each response includes rate limit headers so you can track remaining capacity.

webhooks.quote: Webhooks let Grain push data to your system when events occur, rather than requiring you to poll for changes. Register a webhook URL in your integration and Grain will send a payload to that URL whenever a registered event occurs

sandbox_or_test_env.quote: Is there a sandbox environment for testing? No sandbox is available at this time. Test against your live workspace using a Personal Access Token scoped to your own account to limit exposure.

api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.value: Date-based versions passed via the Public-Api-Version header; support article states current version is 2025-10-31 (the quick-start example shows 2026-10-01). The v1 (beta) API was sunset in September 2026 and v2 is required; versioning is used to introduce/deprecate fields without breaking integrations.
api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.quote: The current API version is `2025-10-31`. All requests must include a `Public-Api-Version` header with this value. Grain uses versioning to introduce and deprecate fields without breaking existing integrations.

verdict_reason: Grain documents a public API whose Personal Access Token is self-serve and "available on every plan, including Free", with OAuth2 also supported for distributed integrations. The API covers reading meeting data, managing/uploading recordings, downloading media, and webhooks, with a documented 300 requests/minute limit. No sales contact, partner approval, or app review is required to obtain a PAT, so a toolkit can be built from documented endpoints alone.
open_questions: No source explicitly labels the API style as REST; it is inferred from documented HTTP endpoints, Bearer-token auth, JSON payloads and versioned endpoint paths (confidence=low).
Official SDKs: no vendor-maintained client libraries are listed in the supplied sources, so sdk_languages is left null.
Community/third-party MCP servers: none appear in the bundle (MCP registry results empty, no GitHub repos checked); absence is unconfirmed.
OAuth2 scope/permission catalog is not shown in the supplied pages; whether scopes are formally documented is unknown.
Version conflict: the support article says the current API version is 2025-10-31 while the developers.grain.com quick-start example sends Public-Api-Version: 2026-10-01.
The official MCP server's concrete endpoint URL is not published in the evidence (only the vendor overview docs page); it may be per-org and client-configured.
Docs index mentions an 'Endpoints — the full API reference' section, but the endpoint count/coverage was not fetched, so api_breadth is approximate.

audit.notes: Authentication page (same S4 article) names three methods: Personal Access Token (PAT, used as 'Authorization: Bearer' in the S3 quick start), Workspace Access Token (WAT, admin + Business/Enterprise), and OAuth2; auth_methods lists these as oauth2 and bearer_token.
audit.mcp_note: Grain's MCP server is described by the vendor as official ('Grain's MCP server is officially supported by us'); value cites the vendor MCP documentation page rather than a concrete endpoint URL.
audit.plan_note: Business plan page lists 'workspace API and webhooks' as a Business feature, consistent with the workspace-token gating while personal PAT access remains free.
